route: The level-two choice lift: an integrality gap engineered from the level-one obstruction, or an exactness theorem on a named class
object: The MERGED MATRIX M(G): at each Max vertex take the componentwise maximum of the two first-passage rows over C u {t1} (equivalently, the one-step law of the branching process in which Max fires BOTH actions at once), together with its frozen variants M^{A,p} and the polyhedral cones K(N) = {D >= 0 : D <= ND} they generate; the level of the choice lift R_j is governed by the transience of these matrices, and the paper owns no such object (its survival operator def:survival takes the max of the two successor VALUES, not of the two rows).
headline: On one-player games the choice lift is governed by a branching process: every x in R_1 satisfies x - w* <= M(x - w*) with M the componentwise max of the two first-passage rows, so R_1 is exact whenever M is transient, R_j is exact whenever freezing some j-1 vertices makes every M^{A,p} transient (in particular whenever fewer than j Max vertices have incomparable rows), and that freezing set is exactly a modulator into a freezing-closed class -- the first exact level, wherever it can be bounded at all, is thm:modulator's number in disguise; and level one is not merely inexact but ASYMPTOTICALLY VACUOUS, on the explicit one-player router tree T_d with only FIVE average vertices, where max_{R_1} x(root) = 1 - Theta(1/N) against w*(root) = kappa, so that T_2(3,1/4) on 14 vertices, one player, already straddles the threshold ([1/4,4/7] around 1/2) where rem:choice-lift's DW needed 27 vertices and two players -- and it does so on a family that thm:few-avg and thm:escape-class both decide outright. The level-two gap was not found: it is proved to require at least two splitters and CR_2 != {0}, and an exhaustive enumeration of the 50625 four-vertex one-player topologies (303750 systems) produced none.

results.name: rl:merge — the merged matrix bounds the level-one relaxation
results.statement: Let G be a stopping SSG with Vmin empty. In the controlled coordinates of lem:transport-dim write x(v^(i)) = p^{v,i}.x + q^{v,i} for the first-passage law of the action (v,i) over C u {t1}, and put M_{v,u} := max(p^{v,0}_u, p^{v,1}_u). Then every x in R_1(G) satisfies D := x - w* >= 0 and D <= MD. Consequently, if M is TRANSIENT (sum_k M^k 1 converges; equivalently rho(M)<1; decided by one exact linear solve) then R_1(G) = {w*}.
results.why_not_implied: rem:choice-lift's only exactness bound is j >= min(|Vmax|, rho_max+1), in terms of the NUMBER of preference-reversing vertices; transience of M is a condition on the ROWS and is incomparable with it — WD(4,2,6) has rho_max = 2 and a non-transient M yet is level-one exact, while the ladder L_n has every vertex reversing and a nilpotent M, so rl:merge decides it and the reversing count says nothing.
results.argument: w* is the least element of Q(G): x in Q means x >= Tx with the sink payoffs carried, so x >= T^k x >= T^k 1_{t1} and the right side increases to w* by thm:lfp-general; hence D >= 0. Fix v. By rem:choice-lift's description of level one, x = lambda Y + (1-lambda) Z with Y in F_v^0, Z in F_v^1. Put P := lambda(Y-w*) >= 0, R := (1-lambda)(Z-w*) >= 0, so P+R = D. Then x(v) = p^{v,0}.P + p^{v,1}.R + lambda(p^{v,0}.w*+q^{v,0}) + (1-lambda)(p^{v,1}.w*+q^{v,1}) <= p^{v,0}.P + p^{v,1}.R + w*(v), because w* in Q(G) (thm:transport-sound) gives w*(v^(i)) <= w*(v). Since P,R >= 0, p^{v,0}.P + p^{v,1}.R <= sum_u max(p^{v,0}_u,p^{v,1}_u)(P_u+R_u) = (MD)(v). For the theorem, 0 <= D <= M^k D <= M^k 1 -> 0. No spectral theory is imported: transience is phrased as convergence of sum_k M^k 1, the least nonnegative solution of y = My + 1.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic throughout (fractions.Fraction; own two-phase simplex mylp.py and exact active-set dual certificates verified entrywise). Predictions checked against the exact first exact level on every instance of the document (table in exact_levels.txt): mu = 0 (M transient) on G8, S, S_r(3), H_3, H_4, H_5 and the ladders L_2..L_6, all level-one exact (the ladders already level ZERO); mu = 1 on W_14, first exact level 2 (rl:merge sharp there); mu = 2 on WD(4,2,6),(6,3,7),(8,4,8), CC(1,2),(2,2),(1,4), CV(1,3),(1,4),(2,4), BC(2,5),(2,6),(3,5), all level-one exact, so the bound is valid but loose. R_1 and R_2 boxes reproduced exactly and agree with the round-17 audit: W_14 R_0 = ([1/2,1],[1/2,1],[15/32,1]), R_1 = ([1/2,3/5],[1/2,23/40],[15/32,11/20]), R_2 = {w*}; G* level-one exact at all seven coordinates; DW level-two exact with the level-one straddle [9/20,11/20]. Also proved level-one exactness of the controlled-cycle family v_i -> (p v_{i+1}, kappa_i) (M = p times a cyclic permutation, transient), confirmed by LP at m = 3,4 and four parameter settings.

results.name: rl:levels and rl:splitters — a freezing set, and incomparable rows, bound the exact level
results.statement: (a) Let G be stopping with Vmin empty, j >= 1, A a subset of C with |A| = j-1, and for p in {0,1}^A let M^{A,p} be M with the row at each c in A replaced by p^{c,p_c}. If M^{A,p} is transient for every p then R_j(G) = {w*}. (b) Call v a SPLITTER if neither p^{v,0} >= p^{v,1} nor p^{v,1} >= p^{v,0} componentwise. If G has at most j-1 splitters then R_j(G) = {w*}; contrapositively, a level-j gap requires at least j splitters, and a game with no splitter is level-one exact.
results.why_not_implied: prop:rows-turn isolates the same incomparability of the two rows but for the CONDITIONED rows p-hat of def:reduced-rows and for a different conclusion — whether the improvement edge at a vertex can turn along the reachability preorder; it bounds no relaxation level, and the two conditions differ whenever the two actions have different self-return probabilities. Nothing there gives R_j = {w*} for any j.
results.argument: (a) For x in R_j with level-j family (z,X), splitting along A gives x = sum_p lambda_p y_p with y_p in F_A^p, and y_p lies in R_{j-|A|} (subset of R_1) because the subfamily indexed by |S|+|T| <= j-|A|, normalised by lambda_p, satisfies every clause of the level-(j-|A|) definition, the extra pins on A only restricting the points. Put P_p := lambda_p(y_p - w*) >= 0; then sum_p P_p = D, and rl:merge-bound applied to y_p gives P_p <= M P_p, while the pin at c in A gives P_p(c) = p^{c,p_c}.P_p + lambda_p(w*(c^(p_c)) - w*(c)) <= p^{c,p_c}.P_p. So P_p <= M^{A,p} P_p and transience forces P_p = 0. (b) Take A to be the set of splitters. Every row of M^{A,p} is then one of the two first-passage rows of its vertex, so M^{A,p} = P_sigma, the first-passage matrix over C of a positional strategy; G stopping makes (P_sigma^k 1)(v), the probability of at least k further visits to C, tend to 0, hence <= 1/2 uniformly for some k_0, and P_sigma^{n k_0} 1 <= 2^{-n} 1: transient.
results.verification: mu := min{|A| : rl:levels applies} computed exactly (topo.py; transience decided by the least-nonnegative-solution test) on every instance: 0 for G8, S, S_r(3), H_m, L_n; 1 for W_14; 2 for WD, CC, CV, BC and for the crossed two-router game D1; 3 for the depth-two router tree; 2^d - 1 for T_d. Splitter counts: 0 for the cycle family and for every leaf of a router tree, 1 for W_14 (sharp: level 2), 2^d - 1 for T_d. Every measured first exact level in exact_levels.txt is <= mu + 1, with equality on W_14, G8, S, S_r(3), H_3, H_4, H_5.

results.name: rl:cone — the cone relaxation CR_j certifies exactness in one linear programme
results.statement: For j >= 1 let CR_j(G) be the set of D in R^C with 0 <= D <= 1 - w* such that for EVERY A of size j-1 there are P_{A,p} >= 0 (p in {0,1}^A) with sum_p P_{A,p} = D and P_{A,p} <= M^{A,p} P_{A,p}. Then {x - w* : x in R_j(G)} is contained in CR_j(G); so CR_j(G) = {0}, one linear programme with O(2^{j-1} binom(|C|,j-1) |C|) rows, proves R_j(G) = {w*}. The criterion is STRICTLY stronger than rl:levels.
results.why_not_implied: def:lasserre-two is a moment (SDP) lift in the value variables and thm:lasserre-vacuous says only that it is vacuous; CR_j is a linear cone relaxation in the DIFFERENCE variable x - w* of a different hierarchy (the choice lift), and it is a sufficient condition for exactness rather than a relaxation of the value — neither statement mentions the other's object.
results.argument: The containment is the display in rl:levels' proof (P_{A,p} := lambda_p(y_p - w*)) together with D <= 1 - w*, which holds because Q(G) lies in the unit box. Strictness: on the four-vertex one-player game D1 with rows v_1 -> (a,b), v_2 -> (a,b), a -> (7/8 v_2, 1/4), b -> (7/8 v_1, 1/4), at every single vertex one of the two freezings leaves a non-transient merged matrix, so rl:levels does not apply at j = 2, while CR_2(D1) = {0}.
results.verification: CR_j computed by exact two-phase simplex (cone.py + mylp.py). CR_1 != {0} and CR_2 = {0} on W_14 — an exact proof of R_2(W_14) = {w*} with no level-two linear programme; CR_1 = {0} on the controlled-cycle family; CR_2 = {0} on D1 and on the five-vertex overlapping-router game D2, both of which have mu = 2, so the criterion is strictly stronger; CR_2 != {0} on the depth-two router tree, on the trees T_d (d >= 2), on the uniform-mixing families and on the three-router cycle D3 — all of which are nevertheless level-two exact, so CR_2 != {0} is necessary and not sufficient. R_2 = {w*} on D1 also confirmed by LP.

results.name: rl:modulator — the certifiable level is a freezing-modulator number
results.statement: For one-player Max stopping games the class M := {G : M(G) transient} is freezing-closed (freezing c to action i replaces the row M_c by p^{c,i} <= M_c and changes no other row) and is a polynomial class (rl:merge makes the level-one linear programme return w* on it). The hypothesis of rl:levels at A says exactly that A is a freezing modulator of G into M in the sense of thm:modulator; hence (first exact level) <= 1 + mu_M(G), and thm:modulator already decides such a game in N^{O(mu_M)}, one power cheaper than the level-(mu_M+1) programme.
results.why_not_implied: thm:modulator is a statement about an abstract freezing-closed target class; it does not identify any class with the transience of a merged matrix, and it says nothing about the Sherali-Adams level of rem:choice-lift. The identification of the two numbers — the smallest freezing set making every merged variant transient, and the level at which rl:levels closes — is what is new, and it is the question rem:choice-lift left open ('is the first exact level the modulator number in disguise?').
results.argument: Freezing-closedness is the displayed inequality on rows plus monotonicity of transience in the entries. Membership in a polynomial class is rl:merge (and, redundantly, thm:one-player — which is exactly why no exactness theorem for one-player games can produce a NEW polynomial class, a limitation stated rather than hidden). The identification of the hypothesis with the modulator condition is by definition, once the frozen game's merged matrix is computed to be M^{A,p}.
results.verification: Checked on the whole table: on every instance where rl:levels certifies exactness at level mu+1, the same set A is a freezing modulator into M of size mu, and thm:modulator's exponent is mu. The relation to thm:escape-class was also examined and is NOT a containment in the polynomial sense: transience of M gives an escape certificate (via the least solution of x = Sx + 1) but with a rate that can be exponentially close to 1; and conversely the escape class does not give level-one exactness — the T_d of rl:tree-vacuous carry escape certificates of polynomial rate (lambda_d = (8d+22)/(8d+23) for e = 3, kappa = 1/4, exact, d = 1..6) and still have a level-one gap.

results.name: rl:tree-vacuous — level one is asymptotically vacuous, on a one-player family with five average vertices
results.statement: For d >= 1, e >= 1 and dyadic kappa let T_d(e,kappa) be the one-player stopping SSG whose Max vertices are the 2^{d+1}-1 nodes of the complete binary tree of depth d, with u -> (u0,u1) at internal nodes and leaf -> (c_1, k_1), where c_1..c_e is the shared average chain c_r -> (root, c_{r+1}), c_e -> (root, t_0) (first-passage law g.e_root, g = 1-2^{-e}) and k_1 heads the shared dyadic chain of value kappa. Then N = 2^{d+1}+e+D+1 and a = e+D average vertices, independently of d; w* = kappa at every Max vertex; max over Q of x(root) = 1. If kappa < g and 2^d(g-kappa) >= 1-kappa then the vector x_ell := 2^d kappa (g + (1-g)2^{-ell})/(2^d kappa + 1 - kappa), indexed by the depth ell, lies in R_1(T_d), so max over R_1 of x(root) >= 2^d kappa/(2^d kappa + 1 - kappa) = 1 - Theta(1/N): level one closes only a Theta(1/N) fraction of the transport interval [kappa,1]. Corollary (rl:tree-threshold): for kappa < 1/2 and 2^d kappa > 1-kappa the level-one interval at the root is [kappa, >= 2^d kappa/(2^d kappa+1-kappa)] and straddles 1/2, so level one does not decide the threshold; the smallest instance is T_2(3,1/4) — 14 vertices, 7 Max, 5 average, w*(root) = 1/4, R_1-interval [1/4, 4/7].
results.why_not_implied: rem:choice-lift records one instance (W_14, max over R_1 of x(v_1) = 3/5 against 1/2, a gap of 1/10 out of a transport interval of 1/2) and one 27-vertex two-player game DW whose level-one interval straddles the threshold by the duality gadget of thm:compare-equivalence. Neither gives a family, neither gives a gap tending to the whole transport interval, and neither gives a one-player straddle; the family here also has a constant number of average vertices, which W_14 (a = 9) and DW (a = 19) do not, so it lies inside thm:few-avg's class and inside the escape class, which rem:choice-lift's witnesses are not known to be.
results.argument: x lies in Q: writing Delta_j := x_{j-1}-x_j = K 2^{-j} with K := 2^d kappa (1-g)/S, S := 2^d kappa + 1 - kappa, one has x decreasing in the depth, x_d - g x_0 = K/2^d = Delta_d, x_d >= kappa (i.e. g >= kappa) and g x_0 >= kappa (the hypothesis). LEAF SPLITS, all realised by one decomposition: put A_ell := (2^d g + 2^d (1-g)2^{-ell} - 1)/(2^d - 1), so A_0 = 1, A_d = g and A is decreasing; hence A in Q, and A(leaf) = g A(root) says A is tight at the feedback action of EVERY leaf, while w* = kappa.1 is tight at every leaf's constant action; with mu := kappa(2^d-1)/S one checks mu A_ell + (1-mu)kappa = x_ell for every ell, so x = mu A + (1-mu) w* is a legal split at every leaf simultaneously. INTERNAL SPLITS: at an internal u of depth ell with children u0,u1 put theta_j := K 2^{-j}, let Y agree with x outside the subtree of u, be x_j + theta_j on the subtree of u0 and x_j - theta_j on the subtree of u1, and let Z be its mirror; then (Y+Z)/2 = x, Y(u) = x_ell = x_{ell+1} + theta_{ell+1} = Y(u0) and Z(u) = Z(u1). Both lie in Q: the order rows read theta_j - theta_{j+1} = K2^{-(j+1)} = Delta_{j+1}, satisfied with equality on both sides; the leaf rows in the lowered subtree read x_d - theta_d >= max(kappa, g x_0), which is exactly x_d - g x_0 = Delta_d = theta_d together with g x_0 >= kappa; and x_j + theta_j = x_{j-1} <= 1.
results.verification: Everything verified in exact rational arithmetic FROM THE BUILT GAME (tgame.py builds the SSG with out-degree two; red.py reduces it; cert_tree.py re-derives the reduced rows from the game and checks x, A, w*, every Y and Z for membership in Q, every pin and every convex identity entrywise). ALL OK for (d,e,kappa) = (1,3,1/2),(2,3,1/4),(3,3,1/4),(4,3,1/4),(2,3,1/2),(3,4,1/8),(2,5,3/8),(5,3,1/4) and, on freshly generated larger instances, (6,3,1/4) with N = 134 and x(root) = 64/67, (7,3,1/8) with N = 263 and x(root) = 128/135, (4,5,3/8) with N = 41 and x(root) = 48/53. The matching UPPER bound max over R_1 = the same value was computed by exact active-set dual certificates for d = 1,2,3 at every coordinate (kappa = 1/2: 2/3, 4/5, 8/9; kappa = 1/4: 2/5, 4/7, 8/11) and in floating point at d = 4 (16/17, 16/19); it is independent of g, as the formula says. T_2(3,1/4) from the game: N = 14, n = 12, stopping, w* = 1/4 at all seven Max vertices, R_1 root interval [1/4,4/7], and max over R_2 of x(root) = 1/4 by an exact dual certificate (game in Tgames.json: 7 max + 5 avg, succ = [(1,2),(3,4),(5,6),(7,10),(7,10),(7,10),(7,10),(0,8),(0,9),(0,12),(12,11),(13,12)], t0 = 12, t1 = 13). Escape certificates computed exactly by policy iteration on x = Sx+1: lambda_d = (8d+22)/(8d+23) and kappa(x_d) = (8d+23)/2 for d = 1..6 at e = 3, kappa = 1/4, matching the proved bound 2^e(d+e)+d+e+1; so the family lies in the escape class with log(1/lambda) = Omega(1/log N). NOT proved: R_2(T_d) = {w*} — exact dual certificates give max over R_2 of x(root) = w*(root) for d = 1,2 and every coordinate for d = 1, five of seven coordinates for d = 2, the rest floating point only.

restatements.label: thm:one-player
restatements.note: that w* is the LEAST element of Q(G) when Vmin is empty — used in every proof above and reproved in two lines from thm:lfp-general — is d'Epenoux's occupancy linear programme, already the content of thm:one-player and prop:oneplayer-lp; it is also why no exactness theorem for one-player games can yield a new polynomial class, which is stated rather than hidden.

restatements.label: rem:choice-lift
restatements.note: min over R_0 = w* on one-player Max games, so every gap in this route is in the max direction: the j = 0 case of the directional halves rem:choice-lift already records.

restatements.label: rem:choice-lift
restatements.note: R_1 = intersection over v of conv(F_v^0 u F_v^1) (Balas' disjunctive closure) is quoted, not reproved.

gap: Missing statement, exactly: there is a stopping simple stochastic game G and a vertex v with max over R_2(G) of x(v) > w*(v). Its negation is target-equivalent (an exact rational linear programme of size N^{O(1)}) and is not conjectured. What this route adds to the search space: by rem:choice-lift such a G has at least three Max vertices, at least three of them reversing; by rl:splitters, if it is one-player, at least two SPLITTERS (Max vertices whose two first-passage rows are incomparable); by rl:levels every single freezing must leave some merged variant non-transient; and by rl:cone, CR_2(G) must differ from {0} — one linear programme, and the binding filter in practice. Two further statements that would settle the shape of the answer and are open here: (i) is R_2 exact on EVERY one-player stopping SSG (which would force a level-two witness to have both players; not target-equivalent, since one-player games are already polynomial by thm:one-player)? (ii) does CR_j(G) = {0} imply a freezing modulator of size j-1 into a freezing-closed polynomial class, i.e. does rl:cone ever certify exactness outside thm:modulator's reach? D1 and D2 have mu = 2 but CR_2 = {0} and still admit a single freezing into the escape class, so the question is untouched by the examples here.
next_steps: 1. The level-two gap, now with a cheap exact filter: enumerate one-player reduced topologies with at least two splitters and CR_2 != {0} (one exact linear programme each), which excludes the whole controlled-cycle family, every game whose merged matrix becomes transient after one freezing, and the crossed two-router families D1, D2; the surviving shapes at |C| = 5,6 were not enumerated here. The uniform-mixing families (every vertex a splitter, merged rows of mass close to 2, mu > 3) are level-ONE exact, so a high splitter count is not the resource — what W_14 and the router trees have and the mixing families lack is a leaf whose two actions are a constant and a feedback, and that is where the next construction should start. 2. Try to prove or refute "R_2 is exact on every one-player stopping SSG". Every attempt here to build a one-player level-two gap failed, and the exhaustive four-vertex enumeration failed; a proof would sharpen rem:choice-lift's barrier to "a level-two witness needs both players". The obstruction to the proof is identified: the bound P <= M^{A,p}P drops the action slacks s_{c,i} = w*(c) - w*(c^(i)), and putting them back (the refined matrix with entries ghat_{c,i} p^{c,i}, ghat = 1 - s/(p.(1-w*)), implemented in topo.mhat) still does not close on the depth-two router tree, which IS level-two exact. 3. The two-player analogue of rl:merge. The proof breaks exactly at D >= 0, which fails as soon as Min vertices are present; the replacement bound D(v) <= (MD)(v) + sum_u L_u |p^{v,0}_u - p^{v,1}_u| with L a level-zero lower bound on Q is valid but additive, and whether it can be iterated into a two-player exactness criterion — which, unlike the one-player case, WOULD be a new polynomial class — was not tried. 4. rl:tree-vacuous asks to be dualised and glued: joining T_d to its dual under thm:compare-equivalence's gadget should make the level-one interval at the root of width 1 - Theta(1/N), i.e. the lift returns nothing at all at level one on a two-player family; the gluing was not computed here.
prior_art: From memory, unchecked against the sources. The hierarchy is Sherali and Adams' reformulation-linearisation technique and level one is Balas' disjunctive closure — both already attributed in rem:choice-lift. The merged matrix M is the mean matrix of a Galton–Watson branching process in which the controller fires both actions at once, and "D <= MD with D >= 0 forces D = 0 when the process is subcritical" is the elementary half of the Perron–Frobenius / Collatz–Wielandt circle; the fifth-theorem rule is respected by phrasing the hypothesis as transience (convergence of sum_k M^k 1, one linear solve), so nothing beyond monotone convergence is used. The gap between max_pi rho(M_pi) and the growth rate of arbitrary products, which is why transience of M is strictly stronger than the escape certificate of def:survival, is Blondel and Nesterov's joint-spectral-radius reading, already cited in the paper. The occupancy linear programme behind "w* is the least element of Q" is d'Epenoux's (prop:oneplayer-lp). The router tree's leaf gadget is lem:dyadic-row, used as stated.
